message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The genes responsible for mane development are expressed strongly in males, leading to the characteristic dark, shaggy fur around their heads and necks. This trait is typically inherited in a dominant fashion, meaning that if a lion inherits the allele for mane growth from either parent, it will usually express the trait.
